**LiFePO4 is the better choice for most buyers.** The sources agree on the main points, though the exact numbers vary from site to site.

**Why LiFePO4 usually wins**
- **Cycle life:** LiFePO4 units are typically rated for 3,000 to 6,000 cycles to 80% capacity. NMC units are rated for roughly 500 to 1,000 cycles in most sources, though one site gives 1,000 to 2,000 ([UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/), [OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/), [PowerStationMatch](https://powerstationmatch.com/learn/lifepo4-vs-nmc)). Compare the end-of-life percentage too, since a rating to 70% promises less than one to 80%.
- **Safety:** When LFP cells fail, they burn cooler and less violently. One lab study found LFP cells released smoke without flames, while all the NMC cells ignited ([UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/), [OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)). LFP is not fireproof, though.
- **Cost per cycle:** LFP is cheaper to make, and the price premium has mostly disappeared. Because LFP lasts several times longer, it usually costs less per cycle ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/), [Enough Watts](https://enoughwatts.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)).

**Where NMC has an edge**
- **Weight:** NMC stores more energy per pound, but the gap is smaller in finished stations than in the cells. One source puts it at about 10% per pound ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)), another at about 16% ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)).
- **Light use:** If you only use the unit a few times a year, the shorter cycle life matters less.
- **Cold weather:** Most manuals block charging below 32°F (0°C) for both chemistries, so chemistry matters less here than some sites suggest ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)).

**Choose NMC only if** weight is your top priority, you'll use the unit rarely, or you already own a working NMC unit. Otherwise, pick LiFePO4 and size it to your needs.

**Example LiFePO4 pick:** The [BLUETTI Elite 200 V2](https://dealectric.com/bluetti-elite-200-v2) is a 2,073.6 Wh LiFePO4 station with a 2,600 W inverter, rated for 6,000+ cycles to 80%, and weighing 24.2 kg (about 53 lb). It has a 5-year warranty and is not expandable. It's aimed at home backup for a fridge, router, and lights, or a weekend in a van. Dealectric lists it at $899, with code AFF5OFF taking $44.95 off. Confirm the code at checkout, since the store has the final say. You can [buy it here](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-200-v2). That is an affiliate link, so Dealectric earns a commission at no cost to you. If you may want more capacity later, look at the expandable AC200L instead.

Sources: [UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/), [OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/), [powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc), [Enough Watts](https://enoughwatts.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc), [PowerStationMatch](https://powerstationmatch.com/learn/lifepo4-vs-nmc), [VoltVanguard](https://volt-vanguard.com/article/lifepo4-vs-nmc-battery-chemistry/), [Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/bluetti-elite-200-v2)
